# Mogharājamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.16 (PTS Snp 216))

**ID:** Snp 5.16 (PTS Snp 216)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Mogharājamāṇavapucchā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mogharājamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Mogharāja", Snp 5.16, PTS Snp 216) is the sixteenth dialogue of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* of the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Hazra 1994]. In this discourse (commencing at verse 1116 in K. R. Norman's numbering), the student Mogharāja asks how one should view the world so as to escape the king of Death [Norman 1997]. The Buddha instructs Mogharāja to look upon the world as void (*suññato*), always remaining mindful, and to eradicate the self-view (*attānudiṭṭhim ūhacca*), by which means one transcends Death [Hazra 1994; Huynh Thi Ha Vy 2015].

 In canonical and post-canonical Pali literature, the text is expounded in the *Cūḷaniddesa* (*Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa*, Cnd 19) and referenced in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4), and *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1).

**Sources**

- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Documented the position of the text within the Sutta Nipāta and summarized the Buddha's advice to Mogharāja on viewing the world as void.
- [Huynh Thi Ha Vy 2015] Huynh Thi Ha Vy, Sunyata from Madhyamaka to Early Yogacara Philosophy (2015) — Quoted the key Pali verse (suññato lokam avekkhassu) on overcoming death through the removal of self-view.
- [Norman 1997] K. R. Norman, The Group of Discourses (Sutta-Nipāta) (1997-2001) — Provided the verse numbering (verse 1116) for Mogharājamāṇavapucchā.
